newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Analysts see Hutchison as unlikely HK Telecom suit.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see Hutchison as unlikely HK Telecom suit.

text.p: Hutchison Whampoa Ltd is an unlikely suitor for Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd both for cost and for regulatory reasons, analysts and regulators say.

Based on Monday's close of HK$14.10, Hongkong Telecom's market capitalisation stood at about HK$152 billion, and taking, for example, a 10 percent stake in the utility would cost HK$15.2 billion, said Kleinwort Benson analyst Nam Park.
"That's a hell of a lot of money, even for Hutchison," Park told Reuters, adding that it was an expensive way to expand Hutchison's own network.
An analyst from a local brokerage also questioned the logic of Hutchison investing in Hongkong Telecom.
"I won't rule it out completely (but) I have my doubts. It's not attractive or logical for them," said the analyst who declined to be named.

He said regulatory issues were also involved, and the office of the Telecommunications Authority (OFTA) would probably oppose consolidation in the industry after its efforts to liberalise the telecom environment in Hong Kong in recent years.
Hongkong Telecom has lost its monopoly on domestic Hong Kong calls. Its monopoly on international calls does not expire until 2006, but competitors are already eating into its margins.
An analyst from a British brokerage said uncertainties over the future of Hongkong Telecom's monopoly also made a Hutchison investment in the utility seem unlikely.
"The monopoly status is valuable, but OFTA is thinking of breaking it up," said the analyst who also declined to be named.
She said Hutchison wanted to invest in its own network.
"They (Hutchison) do have a very strong balance sheet but I'm sure they can think of something else better to put the money towards," she said.
An OFTA spokesman said OFTA would be concerned at one operator which held telecom licences holding a stake in a competing operator which also held licences.
"Our main concern is whether there is concentration of ownership," said OFTA senior assistant director M.H. Au.
Alex Arena head of the telecommunications review with the Government Secretariat, said the rumours surfaced from time to time and he did not want to fuel them by commenting on them.
Arena said the telecom liberalisation in Hong Kong had been aimed at ending up with the most economically efficient industry possible.
"Whether changes in the marketplace achieve that objective or not the government will have to consider at the time," said Arena.
